correctness.rationale: The flow quotient model is established by merging duplicate edges using 0<p<=1 and reducing the 3-edge cycle variable to a concave-between-breakpoints cost; all three spanning trees are considered. Every triple zero-sum molecule has a 2-edge star optimal for p=1; the p<1 quasi-norm obeys the exact 2^{1/p-1} comparison. The dual Lipschitz polytope has exactly six distance-function vertices because all strict triangle inequalities hold, giving Lip(R1)=sec(largest angle/2). At a longest-opposite-side vertex, costs on the two other trees are strictly >2 while star cost=2; explicit small interior perturbation attains matching lower bound. Includes p=1, all shapes and boundary cases; finite numerical checks are auxiliary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Determines the precise shape-sensitive Lipschitz stability of the unique canonical affine interpolation from all Euclidean triangular cells into quasi-Banach free p-spaces of their vertices, throughout an exponent continuum. Such local stability is a mathematically motivated analog of the established cubic interpolation project in Bíma 2023, and the exact angle-bisector extremizer and spanning-tree mechanism distinguish nonlocally convex transport p geometry from the p=1 case. It is neither an arbitrary one-off slice nor an unsupported global triangulation claim. The scalar p=1 component alone is likely classical, but the simultaneous sharp p<1 extension and its geometric dependence carry the value.
